title: Effects of caffeine and sex on muscle performance and DOMS after exercise-induced muscle damage
key_finding: Males showed 21.5% DOMS reduction vs 4.6% in females — first study showing sex difference in caffeine ergogenic effect under EIMD
notes: Double-blind RCT; participants were non-habitual caffeine users (<200 mg/wk)

title: Placebo Effect of Caffeine on Maximal Strength and Strength Endurance in Healthy Recreationally Trained Women Habituated to Caffeine
population: Recreationally trained women habituated to caffeine
key_finding: No placebo effect in habitual caffeine users; belief that caffeine was ingested did not improve performance
notes: Deceptive crossover design; habitual intake 4.1 mg/kg/day; null result paper — important for trap questions

title: Caffeine Increases Muscle Performance During a Bench Press Training Session
population: Young healthy participants (9M, 3F); low caffeine consumers
primary_outcome_measure: Mean bar velocity and power output
primary_outcome_result: Mean velocity +7.8% (p=0.002); mean power +10.1% (p=0.003); total work significantly higher
key_finding: 3 mg/kg caffeine improved muscle performance consistently across all 4 sets of a training session
notes: First study to examine caffeine during a simulated velocity-based workout rather than a test protocol; effect present in 30/32 repetitions

title: Effects of Caffeine Ingestion on Exercise Performance at Low and High Altitudes in Cross-Country Skiers
key_finding: Caffeine effect was significantly greater at high altitude (2900m) than at sea level
notes: Oldest paper in corpus (1982); unique altitude variable; double-blind; ~80% of subjects could distinguish caffeine from placebo

title: Caffeine Ingestion and Isokinetic Strength
population: Male intercollegiate track sprinters; non-caffeine users
primary_outcome_measure: Peak torque and power at varying speeds
primary_outcome_result: No significant effect on peak torque or power at any speed
key_finding: Low dose caffeine (5 mg/kg) showed no ergogenic effect on isokinetic strength under anaerobic conditions
notes: Null result; one of earliest in vivo caffeine + dynamic strength studies; note: dose may have been too low

title: Performance and Metabolic Responses to a High Caffeine Dose During Prolonged Exercise
exercise_type: Running and cycling to exhaustion at ~85% VO2max
primary_outcome_result: Running: 49.2 to 71.0 min (+44%); Cycling: 39.2 to 59.3 min (+51%); both P<0.05
key_finding: High dose caffeine dramatically increased endurance time in both running and cycling; urinary caffeine remained below IOC limit
notes: 9 mg/kg dose is very high; elevated plasma epinephrine twofold; no change in RER or FFA; glycogen-sparing mechanism unclear

title: Dietary Nitrate Supplementation Improves Team Sport-Specific Intense Intermittent Exercise Performance
primary_outcome_result: 4.2% improvement with beetroot juice vs placebo (1704 vs 1636 m; P<0.05)
key_finding: Dietary nitrate (beetroot juice) improved intermittent exercise performance; lower blood glucose and trend for reduced plasma K+ with nitrate
notes: NOT a caffeine paper — intervention is dietary nitrate via beetroot juice; included as contrast/comparison; useful for trap questions about caffeine and team sport

title: The Effects of Different Doses of Caffeine on Endurance Cycling Time Trial Performance
exercise_type: 1-hour cycling time trial (75% peak power output)
primary_outcome_result: 3 mg/kg: 4.2% faster (P<0.05); 6 mg/kg: 2.9% faster (P<0.05); no significant difference between doses
key_finding: Both caffeine doses improved cycling performance; doubling the dose did not improve performance further; 3 mg/kg appears optimal
notes: Double-blind crossover; 56% of participants performed best on 3 mg/kg; dose-response finding challenges assumption that more caffeine = better

title: Physical Exercise in Cancer Patients During and After Medical Treatment: A Systematic Review of Randomized and Controlled Clinical Trials
population: Cancer patients during and after medical treatment
primary_outcome_measure: Physical functioning and health-related quality of life
primary_outcome_result: Positive results observed across diverse outcomes in most trials
key_finding: Exercise benefits cancer patients during and after treatment across physical and psychosocial outcomes
notes: Systematic review — no caffeine; exercise-only; included as contrast paper; very different population from core corpus

title: Effect of Aerobic Exercise on Cognition in Younger Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial
exercise_type: Aerobic exercise 4x/week for 6 months vs stretching/toning
primary_outcome_measure: Executive function (primary) and other cognitive domains
primary_outcome_result: EF improved +0.228 SD at age 40; +0.596 SD at age 60 (P=0.028); effect moderated by age
key_finding: Aerobic exercise improved executive function in younger adults; effect larger in older participants; increased cortical thickness in left frontal region
notes: No caffeine; exercise-only; included as contrast paper; cognitive outcome focus distinguishes it from all other papers
